content: Leaf spot appears as brown or black circular spots on leaves. Remove infected leaves, avoid overhead irrigation, improve spacing between plants, and consult agricultural experts before applying fungicides.
Leaf spot spreads faster in humid environments. Maintain field hygiene, remove fallen infected leaves, and monitor nearby crops regularly.
Leaf blight causes yellowing and drying of leaves. Use disease-free seeds, improve air circulation, avoid excessive watering, and seek expert guidance before chemical treatment.
Leaf blight management includes early detection, pruning infected leaves, crop rotation, and using resistant crop varieties when available.
The crop appears healthy. Continue balanced irrigation, nutrient management, proper sunlight exposure, and regular monitoring for early disease detection.
Healthy crops should be monitored weekly for pest infestation, nutrient deficiency, and environmental stress conditions.
Fungal infections often increase during rainy seasons. Ensure proper airflow, avoid water accumulation, and remove infected plant material immediately.
Pest damage can reduce crop productivity significantly. Monitor leaves regularly, use integrated pest management practices, and avoid overuse of pesticides.
